blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At work, we often ask for help. The most polite way in English is with two small words: "can" and "please".

We say: Can you help me, please? Can I have the report, please? These words are simple. But they are polite, and they make a big impact.

Today you learn 5 important words. We go step by step. You can do it!

items.q: What two words make a request polite in English?
items.why: "the most polite way… is with two small words: 'can' and 'please'."

items.q: "Can you help me, please?" is an example of…
items.why: É um pedido educado — exatamente o que o texto ensina.

items.q: How many important words will you learn today?
items.why: "Today you learn 5 important words."

items.q: Which idea would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Small words can be very polite.
You can learn step by step.
"Please" is not necessary to be polite.
items.why: Inferência: o texto todo diz que "please" é justamente o que torna o pedido educado.

items.q: "You can do it!" at the end suggests the author is…
items.why: Inferência: o tom é de incentivo — o autor motiva o aluno.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie falar sobre o dia dela no trabalho. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Hi, I am Sophie. I work in a small office with a nice team. In the morning, I say good morning to everyone. Then we start work.

I ask for help every day. I say: Can you help me, please? My colleague Tom is very kind. He always says: Yes, of course!

Sometimes I need a file. I say: Can you send the file, please? Tom sends it fast. Thank you, Tom! When I have a good link, I say: Can you share the link with the team, please?

In meetings, I do not understand every word. So I say: Can you repeat, please? Or: Can you speak slowly, please? My team is patient. They repeat for me, and that is okay.

At the end of the day, I say: Thanks a lot! "Please" and "thank you" are small words. But they help me a lot at work, and my team likes them too.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Where does Sophie work?
items.why: "I work in a small office with a nice team."

items.q: What does Sophie say when she needs help?
items.why: "I say: Can you help me, please?"

items.q: What does Sophie say in meetings when she does not understand?
items.why: "So I say: Can you repeat, please? Or: Can you speak slowly, please?"

items.q: How is Sophie's team?
items.why: Inferência: Tom é "very kind" e o time é "patient" — repetem para ela.

items.q: Why does Sophie use "please" and "thank you"?
options: Because they help her a lot at work
items.why: Inferência: "they help me a lot at work, and my team likes them too."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Can you ___ me with this box, please? It is heavy."
items.why: Help = ajudar. A caixa é pesada, então ela pede ajuda.

items.q: "Please send the email now." To send means to…
options: make something go to a person
items.why: Send = enviar: fazer algo chegar a alguém.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Can you ___ the photo with the team, please?"
items.why: Share = compartilhar a foto com o time.

items.q: "Can you repeat that, please?" This means…
items.why: Repeat = repetir: dizer de novo.

items.q: "We say please to be…"
items.why: Please = por favor: usamos para ser educados.

blocks.instruction: Expressões simples que usamos no trabalho para pedir com educação. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Can you send over the file, please?" To send over means to…
items.why: Send over = mandar algo para alguém.

items.q: "Can you help out with the boxes, please?" To help out means to…
items.why: Help out = dar uma ajuda, colaborar.

items.q: "Can you speak up, please? I can't hear you." To speak up means to…
items.why: Speak up = falar mais alto.

items.q: "Please sit down. The meeting starts now." To sit down means to…
items.why: Sit down = sentar-se.

items.q: "Can you write down the number, please?" To write down means to…
items.why: Write down = anotar, escrever no papel.
